record.original_question: For each positive integer n, what is the smallest triangle that can contain n circles of radius 1 without overlap?

evidence.quote: Problem 4. For each n ∈ N, find the smallest triangle in which you can package n circles of radius 1. By package we mean that the n circles must be completely contained in the the triangle without overlapping.

artifact.self_contained_problem: For each positive integer $n$, determine the triangle of smallest area (equivalently, smallest scale) that contains $n$ pairwise non-overlapping closed disks of radius $1$ in the Euclidean plane. Here "contains" means each disk lies entirely inside the closed triangular region, and "non-overlapping" means the interiors of the disks are disjoint. The triangle is allowed to be arbitrary (not required to be equilateral or isosceles), and one seeks, as a function of $n$, the infimum of the area (or of a chosen size parameter) of a triangle admitting such a packing, together with the configurations achieving the optimum.
artifact.status_search_result: For the special case of equilateral triangles, optimal packings of n unit circles are proved only for small n (roughly n ≤ 15), with conjectured optima for n up to about 34; the problem is open in general. For arbitrary triangles the question remains unresolved for general n, with only partial results, bounds, and constant-factor approximation methods (e.g., split packing) known.

status_evidence.title: Circle packing in an equilateral triangle - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Optimal solutions have been proven for n ≤ 15, and conjectures are available for n ≤ 34.
status_evidence.claim: Only finitely many small cases are proved optimal; the general problem is open.

status_evidence.title: Split Packing: Packing Circles into Triangles with Optimal Worst-Case Density
status_evidence.snippet: Split Packing yields a constant-factor approximation for packing circles into the smallest non-acute triangle of a given side ratio.
status_evidence.claim: Approximation algorithms exist, but exact optima are not known in general.
